record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: Universal obstruction to Fourier degree recovery
record.original_question: Does there exist a single map f∈C(S^1;S^1), or even f∈VMO(S^1;S^1), such that no summation process whatsoever can recover deg f from the Fourier-modulus data, meaning that for every admissible summation process (σ_{n,ε}) the quantity \sum_{n∈Z} n|a_n(f)|^2 σ_{n,ε} fails to converge to deg f as ε→0?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.8. Does there exist some f ∈ C(S1;S1) (resp., f ∈ VMO(S1;S1)) such that for any summation process (σn,ε), Σ n |an(f)|2 σn,ε does not converge to deg f?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle. For a measurable map $f:S^1\to S^1\subset\mathbb{C}$, write its Fourier series $f(\theta)\sim\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} a_n(f)\,e^{in\theta}$, where $a_n(f)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{S^1} f(\theta)e^{-in\theta}\,d\theta$.

Recall that $\mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$ consists of maps of vanishing mean oscillation taking values in $S^1$; for every $f\in C(S^1;S^1)$ (and more generally $f\in\mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$) the topological degree $\deg f\in\mathbb{Z}$ is well defined, and one has the formal identity $\deg f = \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2$ whenever the series makes sense (e.g., for $f\in H^{1/2}$).

By an admissible summation process we mean a family $(\sigma_{n,\varepsilon})_{n\in\mathbb{Z},\,\varepsilon>0}$ of complex numbers (or real weights) such that for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, $\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}\to 1$ as $\varepsilon\to 0^+$, and such that for every $g\in C(S^1;S^1)$ (resp. every $g\in\mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$) one has $\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(g)|^2\,\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}$ absolutely convergent for each $\varepsilon>0$.

Question: Does there exist a single map $f\in C(S^1;S^1)$ (respectively a single $f\in\mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$) such that for every admissible summation process $(\sigma_{n,\varepsilon})$, the quantity
$$\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2\,\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}$$
fails to converge to $\deg f$ as $\varepsilon\to 0^+$?
artifact.category_tag: Fourier series and topological degree of VMO maps
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in Brezis's recent list of favorite open problems and is rooted in the Brezis–Nirenberg theory of degree for VMO maps and the Korevaar–Brezis line of work "Winding numbers and Fourier series." Available searches turn up the original problem list and related papers, but no publication resolving the existence of such a universal "bad" map $f\in C(S^1;S^1)$ or $f\in\mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Winding numbers and Fourier series (arXiv:1003.5748)
status_evidence.snippet: Brezis-type questions about recovering the degree of S^1-valued maps from Fourier moduli via summation processes.
status_evidence.claim: Background and partial positive results on summation processes; does not resolve the universal-obstruction question.
